name: sol_defi_lending_12
description: Lending protocol logic that can permanently trap a borrower in unrepayable debt
question: The source file in `source` implements borrow/repay functions for a lending protocol, and its repay logic (interest accrual, fee deduction, rounding, token-transfer handling, or a blocking check) can leave a borrower permanently unable to reduce their debt to zero or fully close their loan, trapping them in perpetual debt, excluding cases where repayment is intentionally blocked only for admin-enforced liquidation, sanctioned/blacklisted addresses, or a protocol-wide pause that equally affects all users' actions.
criteria: repay() subtracts a fee from the repay amount using integer division so the remaining debt can never reach exactly zero, leaving a permanent residual balance
the interest-accrual function runs and compounds debt inside repay() before the debt reduction, so a fee or minimum-repay threshold makes debt grow faster than the user can pay it down
repay() calls transferFrom for the full debt amount but the underlying token deducts a transfer fee, so the contract always credits less than the required debt and rejects full repayment
repay() reverts whenever block.timestamp exceeds a fixed maturity/deadline even though the borrower still owes debt, with no path left to close the position afterward
